Rome Statute treaty status: China, Russia, and the US are not signatories

Four principal organs: Presidency (Piotr Hofmanski of Poland); Judicial Divisions (Pre-Trial, Trial, Appeals Chambers); Office of the Prosecutor (OP); Registry
ICC cases are not commenced by individual 'complaint' and lawyers cannot appear as private prosecutors -- only the OP can prosecute

Liability conditions: (1) RS-listed crimes; (2) territory-of-member-state or national-of-member-state nexus; (3) member-state at the relevant time; (4) no 'complementarity'

Bensouda's careful posting of dates intended to satisfy all requirements except complementarity, which remains the active fight

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban demystifies the public reactions to outgoing ICC Chief Prosecutor Fatou Bensouda's last-day (June 14) announcement that she had requested judicial authorization to proceed with an investigation into the Philippine 'war on drugs.' He summarizes the competing framings: Presidential Spokesperson Harry Roque calling it 'legally erroneous... politically motivated... no big deal' based on 'mere hearsay'; the DFA calling it 'deeply regrettable' and 'a blatant violation of the principle of complementarity,' insisting that Justice Secretary Menardo Guevarra's interagency panel be allowed to finish; Edre Olalia of NUPL celebrating 'justice somewhere, somehow'; and Agnes Callamard of Amnesty International calling it 'a moment of hope.' To demystify, he runs a brief on the Rome Statute and the ICC: the RS as the founding treaty (with China, Russia, and the US not signatories); the ICC as the only permanent international court empowered to try and convict individuals, not states, through four organs (Presidency under Piotr Hofmanski; Pre-Trial, Trial, and Appeals Chambers; Office of the Prosecutor; Registry); ICC cases initiated only by the OP via member-state referral, UN Security Council referral, or Pre-Trial Chamber authorization following a preliminary examination; and individual liability requiring a listed crime, a territorial/national-of-member-state nexus, member-state status at the relevant time, and no complementarity. Complementarity means the ICC acts only where the state is 'unwilling or unable to prosecute' through legitimate local investigations. He notes that Bensouda's careful date-selection (July 1, 2016 - March 16, 2019, and even as early as November 1, 2011) was designed to satisfy every requirement except complementarity -- which is exactly why the DFA insists on Guevarra's panel finishing its work. Presidential immunity is a temporary 'unable to prosecute' factor only during the term (the Estrada plunder conviction post-term is the precedent). He concludes that politics aside and legality upfront, Bensouda's bravado is a major leap, but more hurdles abound: progression to charges, arrest, trial, and possible conviction will depend on (1) the PTC's assessment; (2) new Chief Prosecutor Karim Khan's (an eminent Queen's Counsel) follow-through; (3) how the PNP, DoJ, and OMB demonstrate the 'legitimacy' and 'genuineness' of their work; and (4) how the Supreme Court and the entire judiciary uphold their independence and integrity.
